Stage 5 — reconciliation and operations: enable discrepancy detection and read-only investigation first; progressively authorize narrowly scoped recovery commands after audit and safety tests.
Stage 6 — notification projection: move notifications to material order-state events and verify failures cannot alter order state.

Rollback posture: retain reversible routing and disable new consumers before reverting command producers; drain or quarantine outstanding commands and reconcile all side effects before declaring rollback complete. No rollback may discard accepted order, payment, reservation or delivery evidence.

decisions.title: Use coarse-grained domain ownership with asynchronous integration
decisions.selectedOption: Candidate: retain named Order, Inventory, Payment, Fulfilment, Delivery, Notification and Reconciliation ownership boundaries and use durable asynchronous commands and events between them.
alternatives: Synchronous point-to-point coordination for the full order flow.
A shared database with direct cross-domain updates.
Fine-grained microservices for every process step.
Treat Event-Driven as an approved application architecture style without additional review.
decisions.rationale: The scenario already names durable domain systems, requires explicit event boundaries and prohibits a distributed transaction. AIW deterministic analysis recognizes event contracts and replay obligations but marks Event-Driven as inapplicable or infeasible at the reviewed logical-application stage and Service-Based as only weakly feasible. The candidate therefore uses coarse domain services with event-driven integration rather than claiming approval of a distributed style.
tradeoffs: Improves ownership and partial-failure isolation.
Introduces eventual consistency, contract governance and operational reconciliation.
Avoids unnecessary fine-grained deployment boundaries.
Requires human review of adoption preconditions, rollback and operating ownership.
consequences: Each domain owns its store, invariants and event contracts.
Cross-domain progress is visible as pending or compensating.
Transport and consumer operations become material production responsibilities.
This decision remains proposed and cannot establish an approved pattern selection.

decisions.title: Make Order the process manager and authoritative status owner
decisions.selectedOption: Candidate: C-ORD owns the explicit order state machine and coordinates domain commands while each target domain remains authoritative for its local state.
alternatives: Pure event choreography with no end-to-end coordinator.
A central workflow that directly writes all domain databases.
Derive customer status dynamically from all services at query time.
decisions.rationale: EF-FR-001 requires authoritative order status, while compensation and partial failure require a durable place to represent pending and compensating states. An explicit process manager limits ambiguity without creating a distributed transaction.
tradeoffs: Provides a single customer-visible state and clear compensation coordination.
Adds coordinator logic and requires careful separation from domain authority.
May become a bottleneck in change governance if the state machine is not modular and versioned.
consequences: Order stores process state and issued command identifiers.
Domain outcome events drive order transitions.
Order cannot claim a domain side effect succeeded until the owning domain reports it.
Status mappings and terminal-state definitions require business approval.

decisions.title: Use local atomic state and journal writes with idempotent consumers
decisions.selectedOption: Candidate: each domain commits business state and an outbound journal record locally, then publishes asynchronously; consumers use durable inbox or equivalent deduplication state before applying side effects.
alternatives: Write business state and publish to transport as an uncoordinated dual write.
Assume exactly-once delivery from the transport.
Use a distributed transaction across domains and transport.
Rely only on transient in-memory deduplication.
decisions.rationale: This candidate directly addresses lost-event and duplicate-delivery conditions while respecting EF-C-001 and the assumption that each domain can own a durable transactional store.
tradeoffs: Closes the local state-versus-publication gap.
Adds journal relay, inbox storage, cleanup and monitoring.
Provides business-level effective-once behavior but does not make transport delivery exactly once.
consequences: Publication is asynchronous after local commit.
Journal backlog and inbox growth require operating controls.
Every side-effecting handler must define a durable idempotency scope.
Recovery must preserve or reconstruct journal and inbox evidence consistently.

decisions.title: Define idempotency, correlation and ordering in every contract
decisions.selectedOption: Candidate: use immutable commandId and eventId, stable operation idempotency keys, correlationId and causationId, plus aggregateId and monotonic aggregateVersion; assume ordering only within the documented aggregate or partition key.
alternatives: Global ordering for all order-related events.
Timestamp-only conflict resolution.
Consumer-specific identifiers with no shared correlation model.
Best-effort duplicate detection from payload equality.
decisions.rationale: EF-QR-001 and EF-QR-003 explicitly require consistency boundaries, idempotency, ordering assumptions and end-to-end correlation. The scenario states that duplication, delay and reordering are normal conditions.
tradeoffs: Supports deterministic deduplication and gap detection.
Requires envelope governance and persistent processing evidence.
Per-aggregate ordering is simpler than global ordering but consumers must handle cross-aggregate races.
consequences: Consumers reject, buffer or reconcile invalid versions rather than overwriting state.
Schema evolution must retain envelope semantics.
Correlation identifiers must be protected from accidental sensitive-data inclusion.
Retention policy must cover the required deduplication and reconciliation period, which remains unresolved.

decisions.title: Treat indeterminate payment outcomes as a distinct state
decisions.selectedOption: Candidate: persist each payment operation attempt before invocation; after timeout or connection loss, mark the attempt indeterminate and query or reconcile provider state before retrying capture, void or refund.
alternatives: Retry every timeout automatically.
Treat every timeout as a failure and start a new payment operation.
Require synchronous payment availability for order acceptance.
Depend entirely on provider-side duplicate detection without internal evidence.
decisions.rationale: External payment availability is independent and EF-FR-003 prohibits duplicate charging. A timeout does not prove whether the provider applied the operation.
tradeoffs: Reduces duplicate financial side effects.
May leave orders pending while provider state is established.
Requires provider query capability or Finance exception handling.
Cannot guarantee duplicate prevention until the provider idempotency contract is validated.
consequences: Payment has explicit pending, succeeded, rejected and indeterminate attempts.
New operation generations require an explicit business decision.
Finance owns unresolved payment discrepancies.
Capture timing remains an open business decision.

decisions.title: Apply authenticated, least-privilege event and recovery access
decisions.selectedOption: Candidate: use authenticated workload identities, operation-level authorization, encrypted channels, minimized event payloads and separately authorized, audited recovery commands.
alternatives: Trust all workloads connected to the internal network.
Authorize only at transport namespace level.
Include full order and payment objects in every event.
Allow operators to edit domain databases directly.
decisions.rationale: EF-QR-004 requires producer and consumer authentication and protection of sensitive order and payment data. Recovery and replay can create business side effects and therefore need controls equivalent to normal commands.
tradeoffs: Reduces unauthorized publication, consumption and replay.
Adds identity, policy, secret and audit operations.
Payload minimization may require additional authorized domain lookups.
consequences: Every interface has an identity and authorization policy.
Dead-letter and reconciliation evidence receive sensitive-data controls.
Direct database correction is excluded from normal recovery.
Classification and retention details remain subject to Security and data-owner approval.

decisions.title: Require explicit recovery plans and post-recovery reconciliation
decisions.selectedOption: Candidate: each durable domain and the event transport must have a named owner, backup and failover procedure, recovery test, and post-recovery reconciliation gate before production acceptance.
alternatives: Rely on infrastructure defaults without domain reconciliation.
Document recovery after implementation.
Recover stores independently and resume side effects immediately.
decisions.rationale: AIW deterministic finding GOV-RECOVERY-DECISION requires an architecture decision covering backup, failover and recovery testing. Independent recovery can reintroduce duplicate or missing work unless journals, inboxes and business state are reconciled.
tradeoffs: Makes recovery ownership and evidence explicit.
Requires recovery objectives and test investment before handoff.
Post-recovery reconciliation may delay return to normal processing.
consequences: Recovery objectives and topology remain unresolved and require human approval.
Recovery tests must include journal, inbox and external-provider discrepancies.
This candidate decision does not satisfy the deterministic finding until an accepted ADR exists.

decisions.title: Use state-aware cancellation and explicit compensation commands
decisions.selectedOption: Candidate: cancellation is an Order state transition followed by idempotent release, void, refund, warehouse-cancel or delivery-cancel commands selected from an approved compensation matrix; each owner reports the actual result.
alternatives: Delete the order and infer downstream cancellation.
Broadcast one generic cancellation event to all systems.
Treat cancellation as an immediate synchronous transaction.
Allow support staff to alter each system manually without a correlated case.
decisions.rationale: EF-FR-004 requires cancellation semantics, and the scenario lists orphaned reservations and inconsistent cancellation as known risks. Since cross-domain rollback is unavailable, compensation must be explicit and state-aware.
tradeoffs: Makes partial cancellation and too-late outcomes visible.
Requires a business-owned compensation matrix and cut-off rules.
Some outcomes may require operator intervention rather than automatic reversal.
consequences: Order can expose cancellation-requested, compensating, cancelled, partially-cancelled or exception states once the vocabulary is approved.
Inventory, Payment, Fulfilment and Delivery remain authoritative for their cancellation result.
The design is only partially specified until capture timing and cancellation cut-offs are approved.

risks.description: A duplicated or blindly retried payment operation may create a duplicate charge, void or refund.
risks.mitigation: Use persisted payment operation generations, stable idempotency keys, provider references, indeterminate state, provider status queries and Finance reconciliation; validate provider idempotency behavior before production acceptance.

risks.description: Concurrent or duplicate reservation processing may oversell inventory.
risks.mitigation: Make Inventory the sole reservation owner; enforce reservation invariants and version checks in its local transaction; deduplicate commands and reconcile conflicting reservations.
risks.owner: Inventory service owner and Commerce product owner

risks.description: A successful reservation may become orphaned when downstream payment or order processing fails.
risks.mitigation: Track reservationId in Order process state, issue idempotent release compensation, detect aged pending reservations and route unresolved releases to reconciliation.
risks.owner: Inventory service owner and Commerce product owner

risks.description: A committed domain change may have a missing or indefinitely delayed event.
risks.mitigation: Use local transactional journals, monitored relays, durable transport, reconciliation against journal state and tested recovery procedures.

risks.description: Cancellation may be applied inconsistently across Order, Payment, Inventory, Fulfilment and Delivery.
risks.mitigation: Approve a state-based compensation matrix, retain one correlated cancellation case, require each domain to return an explicit outcome and escalate too-late or conflicting states to the named business owner.
risks.owner: Commerce product owner with Finance and Warehouse operations

risks.description: Duplicate or out-of-order events may regress projections or trigger repeated side effects.
risks.mitigation: Use immutable eventId, durable consumer inboxes, aggregate versions, gap detection and idempotent side-effect handlers; route unresolved gaps to reconciliation.

risks.description: Independent payment or carrier outages may leave external operation outcomes unknown.
risks.mitigation: Persist external attempts and references, use status-query reconciliation, isolate retries and expose indeterminate state to operators and customers where material.

risks.description: Sensitive order or payment information may be exposed through event payloads, logs, traces, dead-letter records or operator views.
risks.mitigation: Classify and minimize payloads, exclude credentials, encrypt data, mask telemetry, restrict subscriptions and recovery access, and audit sensitive evidence access.

risks.description: Retry storms, poison events or transport backlog may delay fulfilment and obscure stuck work.
risks.mitigation: Use isolated subscriptions, bounded retries, dead-letter routing, backpressure, backlog visibility and runbooks; require domain owners to classify and remediate poison events.

risks.description: Recovery objectives, failover design and recovery-test ownership are not approved.
risks.mitigation: Accept an ADR defining recovery objectives, backup and failover ownership, test cadence and post-recovery reconciliation before production handoff.
risks.owner: SRE with all domain store owners

delivery.executiveSummary: This candidate package proposes coarse-grained domain ownership with durable asynchronous commands and events, an Order-owned process manager, local transactional journals, idempotent consumers, explicit payment ambiguity, state-aware compensation and controlled reconciliation. It satisfies the no-distributed-transaction constraint by making every domain transition local and cross-domain progress eventually consistent. AIW deterministic analysis supports explicit event contracts and recovery obligations but does not approve Event-Driven as the logical-application style; therefore no pattern or production status is claimed. Production handoff remains blocked by unresolved state, compensation, provider, security-retention and recovery decisions.

sddSections.heading: Architecture style and boundaries
sddSections.content: Candidate domain services own Order, reservation, payment, warehouse work, delivery, notification and reconciliation state. Event-driven integration is used between coarse-grained boundaries, but no approved microservices or Event-Driven application-style selection is asserted.

sddSections.heading: Consistency and contracts
sddSections.content: Each domain commits only its local state. Local journals close the state-publication gap; durable inboxes provide business-level idempotency. Commands have one named owner, events report immutable facts, and ordering is assumed only for the documented aggregate key.

sddSections.heading: Fulfilment coordination
sddSections.content: Order durably coordinates reservation, payment and work creation while exposing pending and compensating states. Inventory, Payment, Fulfilment and Delivery remain authoritative for their own outcomes. Cancellation invokes explicit, idempotent compensations rather than rollback.

sddSections.heading: Failure and reconciliation
sddSections.content: Retries are limited to operations classified as safe. Poison messages use dead-letter and operator cases. Payment and carrier timeouts become indeterminate states and require provider lookup or reconciliation. Recovery preserves journal, inbox and business evidence.

sddSections.heading: Security and operations
sddSections.content: All producers, consumers, external adapters and operators require authenticated identities and operation-level authorization. Sensitive payloads are minimized, recovery actions are separately authorized and audited, and direct database correction is excluded.

sddSections.heading: Governance status
sddSections.content: All records are candidate proposals. AIW review identified missing accepted ADRs and an explicit recovery decision. State vocabulary, compensation policy, provider behavior, recovery objectives and deployment topology require human approval before implementation handoff or production acceptance.

openIssues: Approve the customer-visible order state machine and terminal states.
Approve sequencing among inventory reservation, payment authorization, capture and warehouse release.
Approve the compensation matrix, including void versus refund and manual-exception conditions.
Confirm payment and carrier idempotency and status-query contracts.
Define warehouse and carrier cancellation cut-offs.
Define retry limits, dead-letter escalation, event retention and replay authorization.
Define data classification, event payload allowlists, masking and retention.
Define deployment topology, capacity assumptions and failure-domain placement.
Define recovery objectives, backup and failover procedures, test cadence and owners.
Create and accept ADRs for style, integration, data ownership, security, resilience, compensation and recovery.
Resolve the AIW compatibility-projection warning through explicit architect materialization if a canonical Design Graph is required.
implementationRoadmap: Approve the governance baseline and record candidate decisions as human-reviewed ADRs without treating this package as acceptance.
Build the authoritative Order API, state history and idempotent order acceptance.
Introduce versioned envelopes, local journals, relays, inboxes, correlation and transport operations.
Integrate Inventory reservation and release, proving concurrency and duplicate-command invariants.
Integrate Payment using persisted attempts and an indeterminate-state workflow before enabling capture or refund automation.
Integrate Fulfilment and Delivery with state-aware cancellation and provider reconciliation.
Enable read-only reconciliation and correlated support views, then progressively authorize narrowly scoped recovery commands.
Move notifications to material state events and verify notification isolation.
Run failure injection, security, replay and recovery tests; reconcile all open exceptions before cutover.
Use reversible routing and controlled consumer enablement; do not retire legacy paths until accepted orders and side effects reconcile.
acceptanceAndFitnessTests: Order idempotency: submit the same create-order request and idempotency key more than once; verify one authoritative order and the same recorded result are returned.
Local publication recovery: stop an event relay after committing domain state, restore it, and verify the journal publishes the fact without losing the state or repeating the logical side effect.
Consumer deduplication: deliver the same reservation, payment, fulfilment and notification message more than once; verify each domain records one logical outcome.
Ordering: deliver a later aggregate version before an earlier version; verify the consumer does not regress state and creates the configured gap or retry evidence.
Payment ambiguity: interrupt a capture response after provider submission; verify Payment enters indeterminate state and does not issue a blind second capture before query or reconciliation.
Oversell protection: execute conflicting reservation commands against the same constrained inventory state; verify Inventory preserves its approved reservation invariant.
Compensation: simulate inventory success followed by payment rejection; verify the order becomes compensating and an idempotent reservation release is issued and correlated.

Cancellation race: request cancellation while fulfilment or delivery advances; verify the owning domain returns an explicit cancelled, too-late, completed or operator-required result and Order exposes the mapped status.
Poison event: provide a schema-valid message that repeatedly fails business handling; verify bounded retry, dead-letter isolation, alert evidence and a correlated operator case.
Notification isolation: force notification dispatch failure and verify authoritative order state does not roll back.
Authorization: attempt command publication, event subscription and recovery replay using unauthorized identities; verify denial and audit evidence.
Sensitive-data control: inspect representative events, logs, traces, dead-letter records and operator views; verify prohibited payment credentials and unapproved customer fields are absent or masked.

Traceability: select an order and verify its API request, commands, events, domain transitions, provider attempts, compensations and operator actions can be correlated without exposing prohibited data.
Recovery: restore each domain store and event transport under the approved recovery plan, then verify journal, inbox, domain state and external-provider reconciliation before side effects resume.
ADR coverage: verify every selected major style, integration, data, security, resilience, compensation and recovery choice has a proposed or accepted ADR before implementation handoff.

abstentions: No throughput, latency, availability, retention, retry-count, recovery-time or recovery-point guarantee is proposed because calibrated targets were not supplied.
No cloud, broker, database, workflow engine, observability or identity product is selected.
No regulatory classification or compliance obligation is inferred.
No provider idempotency, status-query or cancellation capability is assumed until contract evidence is supplied.
No architecture pattern, ADR, production handoff or Design Graph materialization is approved by this package.
No payment capture timing or automatic compensation rule is invented.
unsupportedClaimsRejected: The compatibility Design Graph projection is not treated as a canonical architect-approved graph.
The architecture review score and readiness percentages are not treated as production approval.
The Core ledger appearing in deterministically derived journeys is not treated as a real scenario dependency without confirmation.
Deterministic ranking of Event-Driven, Service-Based or any other style is not treated as an accepted architecture decision.
Small-team, restricted-data and high-regulatory-exposure calibration assumptions are not asserted as scenario facts.
Pattern evidence listed by the review is not treated as an accepted governed pattern selection.

problemUnderstanding.businessObjective: Provide governed multi-source analytics to authorised BI and model consumers while protecting personal information and preserving source ownership, reproducible lineage, jurisdictional placement and complete audit evidence.
scope: Governed onboarding of batch and change-data-capture sources.
Region-aware ingestion, protected landing, transformation and data-quality validation.
Cataloguing, classification, lineage capture and analytical-product publication.
Role-, purpose-, classification- and jurisdiction-aware BI and model access.
Masking, tokenisation, encryption and controlled export across trust boundaries.
Retention, legal hold, deletion and associated evidence.
Monitoring, incident response and recovery of data, lineage and access policy.
Operational source systems remain authoritative; analytical copies are not operational systems of record.
journeys: A source owner registers a source contract, ownership, classification, jurisdiction and extraction semantics before ingestion is enabled.
The ingestion plane validates a batch or CDC delivery, records source position and ownership, and either lands it in the permitted region or quarantines it with a classified failure.
The processing plane transforms and quality-checks data, records code, configuration and input lineage, and publishes only certified analytical products.

An analyst discovers a permitted product and submits a BI query; access is evaluated from identity role, declared purpose, dataset policy, classification and jurisdiction before data is filtered or masked.
A data scientist requests governed feature access; the same policy and audit controls apply to model consumption and export.
A lifecycle action evaluates retention and legal hold, propagates an authorised deletion through raw, derived and cached copies, and records completion or unresolved residues.
An auditor obtains correlated evidence for access, transformation, policy decisions, exports, holds and deletions without receiving unrestricted access to analytical data.
SRE restores a data product in a permitted region and verifies source checkpoints, lineage, classification and access policy before reopening consumption.
The deterministic JNY-001 identity journey is retained only as unresolved input because its Customer and Core ledger participants do not align with the supplied sensitive-analytics scenario.

qualityDrivers.statement: Classify, encrypt, mask or tokenise sensitive fields across trust boundaries.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Direct and indirect identifiers create re-identification and disclosure risks at ingestion, processing, consumption and export boundaries.

qualityDrivers.statement: Enforce regional or jurisdictional data-placement constraints.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Placement policies vary by dataset and consumer purpose, so location must be evaluated as policy rather than assumed from a single platform default.

qualityDrivers.statement: Detect data-quality, lineage and pipeline-health failures.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Consumers require distinguishable evidence of freshness, quality and provenance rather than silent delivery of stale or uncertified products.

qualityDrivers.statement: Recover analytical data products without losing source lineage or access policy.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Restoring data alone could expose an unclassified or incorrectly authorised product; metadata and policy must be restored and validated with it.

qualityDrivers.statement: Preserve complete access, transformation and export audit evidence.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Auditability is a primary business objective and must cover both data-plane activity and control-plane changes.

qualityDrivers.statement: Keep operational source systems authoritative.
qualityDrivers.rationale: The analytical platform must support rebuild and deletion without becoming the operational system of record.

constraints: Some records contain direct and indirect identifiers.
Jurisdiction policies vary by dataset and consumer purpose.
Analytical stores are not systems of record for operational source data.
Human approval is required before any proposed decision, pattern or graph materialisation becomes authoritative.
The current Design Graph is a compatibility projection rather than an architect-materialised canonical graph.
No quantitative availability, recovery, freshness or retention target was supplied.
assumptions: Source owners expose change or extract contracts.
A governed identity platform provides workforce attributes.
ambiguities: Dataset-specific jurisdictions, permitted transfer routes and consumer-purpose rules are not enumerated.
The authoritative vocabulary and approval process for consumer purposes are not defined.
The threshold for treating combinations of indirect identifiers as sensitive is not defined.
Retention periods, legal-hold authorities and precedence rules are not supplied.
The meaning, storage duration and admissibility criteria for complete audit evidence are not specified.
Recovery tiers, recovery objectives and permitted recovery regions are not supplied.
Source replay, ordering, late-arrival and schema-evolution semantics are not specified per source.
The AIW context contains an open duplicate candidate between REQ-001 and REQ-002 that requires human adjudication.
The deterministic JNY-001 and system-context candidate reference Customer and Core ledger, which conflict with the supplied identity and analytics context.
The deterministic style evaluation found only Service-Based eligible, with weak feasibility; it did not approve an architecture style or pattern.
unresolvedQuestions: Which jurisdiction and residency rules apply to each dataset, derived product and consumer purpose?
Who approves the purpose vocabulary and exceptional access?
Which fields require masking, irreversible transformation, reversible tokenisation or access denial?
What are the retention schedules, legal-hold authorities and deletion-evidence requirements?
What recovery objectives and source replay windows apply to each analytical product?
May any metadata, token mapping, backup or audit record cross a dataset's regional boundary?
What source ordering, deduplication, late-arrival and schema-compatibility contracts are guaranteed?
Which exports are permitted, who approves them and how must downstream deletion be evidenced?
Should REQ-001 and REQ-002 be consolidated while preserving both provenance chains?
Should the inconsistent JNY-001 and compatibility system-context projection be replaced with scenario-aligned journeys before canonical graph materialisation?

systemContext: Source systems are external systems of record. Each integration is governed by a source owner and a versioned extract or change contract.
The sensitive analytics platform contains region-scoped ingestion, protected storage, processing, catalog, policy, privacy, lifecycle, audit and recovery capabilities.
The governed identity platform supplies workforce identity attributes; the analytics platform does not infer missing attributes.
BI and model platforms are external consumers that access data only through governed query or feature interfaces.
Data owners and stewards own datasets, classification and quality disposition; privacy and security own control policy; SRE owns runtime recovery; auditors consume segregated evidence.
Primary trust boundaries are source-to-ingestion, ingestion-to-protected landing, processing-to-published product, platform-to-consumer, control-plane-to-data-plane and every jurisdictional boundary.
Cross-region data, metadata, backups, token mappings and audit movement are denied unless the applicable dataset and purpose policy explicitly permits them.

components.name: Source Contract and Intake Registry
components.description: Registry for source ownership, schemas, extraction semantics and required governance metadata.
components.responsibility: Require a named source owner and versioned batch or CDC contract, then approve or reject onboarding prerequisites before data movement begins.

components.name: Regional Ingestion Plane
components.description: Region-scoped adapters and checkpoints for governed batch and CDC intake.
components.responsibility: Authenticate sources, validate contracts, preserve source positions, route records to permitted regional landing areas and quarantine invalid deliveries.

components.name: Protected Landing and Quarantine Store
components.description: Region-bound storage for encrypted source snapshots, change sets and rejected records.
components.responsibility: Preserve replayable source inputs and failure evidence without representing them as certified analytical products or operational records.

components.name: Transformation and Data-Quality Orchestrator
components.description: Controlled execution plane for reproducible transformations and quality gates.
components.responsibility: Execute versioned transformations, record input and output identities, evaluate quality rules, isolate failures and publish only products that pass required gates.

components.name: Catalog, Classification and Lineage Service
components.description: Governed metadata service for dataset identity, ownership, classification, policy references and lineage.
components.responsibility: Maintain source-to-product lineage and certification state, expose only authorised metadata and prevent publication when required lineage is incomplete.

components.name: Policy Decision and Administration Service
components.description: Policy control plane using identity, role, purpose, classification, jurisdiction and lifecycle attributes.
components.responsibility: Maintain governed policies and return an allow, deny or indeterminate decision with applicable row, column, masking, export and regional obligations.

components.name: Governed Analytical Store
components.description: Region-scoped storage for certified analytical products and derived features.
components.responsibility: Store versioned analytical copies, enforce policy obligations at query time and retain source and lineage references while remaining non-authoritative for operational facts.

components.name: Governed BI and Model Access Gateway
components.description: Common enforcement boundary for BI queries, model feature access and controlled exports.
components.responsibility: Authenticate consumers, capture declared purpose, obtain policy decisions, apply filtering or masking, label outputs and produce correlated access and export audit events.

components.name: Privacy Protection and Key Service
components.description: Region-aware cryptographic, masking and tokenisation capability.
components.responsibility: Manage encryption boundaries and approved field transformations while isolating keys and reversible token mappings from general analytics workloads.

components.name: Retention, Legal-Hold and Deletion Coordinator
components.description: Lifecycle control plane for raw, derived, cached and exported analytical copies.
components.responsibility: Evaluate retention and hold policy, issue idempotent lifecycle actions, track propagation and record completed, blocked or unresolved deletion outcomes.

components.name: Audit Evidence Service
components.description: Segregated evidence store for access, policy, transformation, administration, export and lifecycle activity.
components.responsibility: Correlate append-only evidence, detect gaps, restrict evidence access and support auditor retrieval without granting unrestricted analytical-data access.

components.name: Operations, Monitoring and Recovery Control Plane
components.description: Operational control plane for pipeline health, placement drift, backups, restore and controlled reopening.
components.responsibility: Detect failures, coordinate permitted-region recovery and verify restored data, lineage, classification and policy before consumption resumes.

interfaces.name: Governed Batch or CDC Intake
interfaces.owner: Source-system owner with Data owner oversight
interfaces.contract: Versioned schema and extraction contract carrying source identity, source position or extract identifier, ownership and dataset routing metadata.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Duplicate deliveries are handled idempotently using source identity and position. Contract, schema, authentication or placement failures are quarantined; the durable checkpoint is not advanced and the source owner is notified.
securityControls: Malware or content inspection where applicable

interfaces.name: Workforce Identity Attributes
interfaces.contract: Authenticated identity assertion containing governed workforce attributes required by the current policy version.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Missing, expired, contradictory or unavailable identity attributes produce an indeterminate decision that is treated as deny. The analytics platform does not infer or reconstruct attributes.
securityControls: Audit of authentication and policy correlation

interfaces.name: Regional Protected Landing
interfaces.contract: Authenticated write of an encrypted source batch or change segment with source checkpoint, contract version, classification and jurisdiction metadata.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: A checkpoint becomes eligible to advance only after durable landing and metadata correlation succeed. Integrity or storage failures pause the affected feed and preserve the last confirmed checkpoint.
securityControls: Encryption in transit and at rest

interfaces.name: Transformation Stage Contract
interfaces.contract: Versioned input manifest containing immutable input identifiers, source positions, schema version, transformation version and required quality rules.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Stages are restartable from recorded inputs. Failed quality or transformation execution produces no certified publication; failed records and diagnostics remain isolated for steward disposition.

interfaces.name: Lineage and Certification Publication
interfaces.contract: Atomic publication request containing input lineage, transformation and configuration versions, output identity, quality result, classification and policy references.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: If required lineage or certification metadata cannot be persisted, the product remains unpublished even if data processing completed. Retrying uses the same product and lineage identities.

interfaces.name: Policy Evaluation
interfaces.owner: Security with Privacy officer and Data owner policy approval
interfaces.contract: Request containing subject attributes, dataset and product identifiers, declared purpose, action, region and export context; response is allow, deny or indeterminate with enforcement obligations and policy version.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Indeterminate, unavailable or expired policy decisions are denied. Cached decisions must not outlive their validity or bypass a hold, revocation or policy change.

interfaces.name: Governed BI Query
interfaces.contract: Authenticated query request containing consumer identity, declared purpose, product identifier and requested operation; response is filtered or masked data, denial, or classified failure.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: A query executes only after a valid policy decision and audit correlation are established. Policy, audit or masking failure denies the request rather than returning unprotected data.

interfaces.name: Governed Model Feature Access
interfaces.owner: Model platform owner with Data owner oversight
interfaces.contract: Authenticated feature request containing model workload identity, approved purpose, product version and requested feature set.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Uncertified, stale-policy, unapproved-purpose or regionally incompatible requests are denied. Partial feature retrieval must not silently substitute a different version or classification.

interfaces.name: Lifecycle Action
interfaces.owner: Data owner with Privacy officer oversight
interfaces.contract: Idempotent retain, hold, release-hold or delete instruction carrying dataset or subject scope, policy basis, authorised actor and correlation identifier.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: An applicable legal hold blocks deletion and records the blocked outcome. Partial deletion is retried and remains visibly unresolved until every in-scope copy reports completion or an authorised exception is recorded.

interfaces.name: Correlated Audit Event
interfaces.contract: Structured event containing actor or workload identity, action, object, purpose where applicable, policy and transformation versions, outcome, region, timestamp and correlation identifier without unnecessary sensitive payloads.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Events are durably buffered in the permitted region. If required evidence cannot be accepted and buffering cannot continue, protected access, export, lifecycle action or product publication stops rather than creating an unaudited success.
securityControls: Encryption in transit and at rest

interfaces.name: Privacy Transformation and Key Operation
interfaces.contract: Approved cryptographic, masking or tokenisation operation carrying field classification, dataset region, transformation policy and authorised workload identity.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: An unavailable key, invalid policy or region mismatch stops the affected ingestion, processing or access path. There is no plaintext or unmasked fallback.
securityControls: No key material in application logs

interfaces.name: Controlled Restore and Reopen
interfaces.contract: Authorised restore plan identifying dataset version, permitted target region, source checkpoint, metadata set, policy version and validation evidence.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Restore occurs only in a permitted region. Failed integrity, lineage, classification, audit-reference or policy validation leaves the product closed to consumers and triggers escalation.

interfaces.name: Authorised Catalog Discovery
interfaces.contract: Metadata search request carrying authenticated identity and declared purpose; results contain only products and metadata fields the requester may discover.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Catalog unavailability returns a classified discovery failure and does not permit direct store discovery or policy bypass. Stale certification state prevents new consumption until reconciled.

dataArchitecture: Each dataset manifest records a stable dataset identity, source system, source owner, data owner, steward, schema and contract versions, classification, jurisdiction, permitted purposes, retention and hold references, authoritative-source locator and analytical-copy status.

Operational facts remain authoritative in source systems. Analytical products carry source checkpoints or extract identifiers and can be rebuilt without presenting the analytical store as the operational record.
Protected landing, quarantine, certified products, metadata, backups and audit evidence are partitioned by applicable placement policy; cross-region replication is a separately authorised action.

Transformation outputs are versioned and linked to immutable input manifests, executable transformation version, configuration version and quality results. Publication requires complete lineage and certification metadata.
Direct and indirect identifiers are classified at intake and reassessed for derived products. Approved masking, tokenisation or minimisation policy is attached to fields and consumption purposes.

Reversible token mappings and cryptographic keys are separated from analytical data and remain within their permitted jurisdiction. General analysts and processing workloads cannot retrieve mapping material.
Retention, hold and deletion apply to raw, derived, cached and controlled exported copies. Lifecycle state includes pending, blocked-by-hold, completed and unresolved outcomes.
Audit records correlate access, policy decisions, transformations, administrative changes, exports and lifecycle operations while excluding unnecessary sensitive payloads.
Certified product freshness and quality state are explicit metadata. Consumers must not silently receive an uncertified product or substitute version.
Backup manifests include data version, source checkpoint, lineage graph reference, classification, policy version, key reference and audit correlation needed to validate a restored product.
securityArchitecture: Use a default-deny attribute-based access model combining workforce role, declared purpose, dataset ownership policy, classification, action and jurisdiction; role alone is insufficient.
Separate policy administration, policy decision, data access, key management, lifecycle administration and audit retrieval duties.
Encrypt data in transit and at rest, with region-aware key use and no plaintext fallback when cryptographic services fail.
Apply data minimisation, field suppression, masking or tokenisation before data crosses into a less-trusted consumer boundary.
Treat BI result download, model feature extraction and bulk query as exports requiring explicit policy evaluation and audit evidence.
Authenticate every human and workload interface; use short-lived, scoped identities and deny missing or indeterminate identity attributes.
Record and review privileged policy, classification, key, hold, deletion and recovery changes independently of the administrator performing the action.
Prevent sensitive values, keys and token mappings from entering logs, traces, failure messages or lineage payloads.
Restrict catalog visibility because dataset names, schemas, classifications and lineage can themselves reveal sensitive information.
Continuously compare observed data, metadata, backups and endpoints against expected regional placement and block unauthorised movement.
deploymentRuntime: Deploy data-plane components as region-scoped cells selected by dataset placement policy; do not assume that failover to another region is lawful.
Keep landing, analytical storage, token mappings, keys, required audit evidence and backups in the permitted region unless an explicit policy authorises movement.
Use coarse-grained platform services with explicit contracts rather than adopting fine-grained distributed deployment by default. This remains a candidate decomposition, not an approved pattern.
Separate production data-plane identities from policy administration, observability, delivery automation and recovery identities.
Apply infrastructure and policy configuration through versioned, reviewable deployment artifacts so runtime placement and access policy can be reconciled with intended state.
Replicate control metadata only after classifying it and applying the same placement rules as the dataset when metadata could reveal sensitive information.
Run ingestion and processing independently per source or product failure domain so one quarantined feed does not require bypassing controls for other feeds.
No deployment topology is production-approved until the canonical Design Graph, owners, recovery decision and dataset policy matrix are accepted.
resilienceFailurePaths: Source unavailable: retain the last confirmed source checkpoint, mark downstream freshness state, alert the source owner and do not fabricate or silently advance data.
Schema or contract violation: quarantine the delivery, preserve diagnostics without leaking sensitive payloads and prevent checkpoint advancement.
Duplicate or replayed delivery: use source identity and checkpoint semantics to process idempotently and retain correlation evidence.
Data-quality failure: prevent certification and publication, preserve the last certified version and route the failure to the steward.
Lineage service unavailable: processing may remain isolated in staging, but no product is certified or exposed until lineage persistence succeeds.
Identity or policy service unavailable: deny new protected actions and do not extend an expired or invalid decision.
Privacy or key service unavailable: stop the affected path; never fall back to unencrypted, unmasked or detokenised data.
Audit service impaired: use permitted-region durable buffering; if required evidence cannot be retained, block publication, access, export and lifecycle success.
Lifecycle partial failure: keep the action unresolved, retry idempotently, prevent a false completion record and escalate residual copies.
Regional outage: restore or fail over only to a region allowed for the dataset and purpose; otherwise keep the product unavailable.
Restore validation failure: keep the product closed until data integrity, lineage, classification, policy and audit references are reconciled.
Catalog inconsistency: prevent discovery or new consumption of affected products while retaining evidence and escalating reconciliation.

Monitor transformation outcomes, quality-rule failures, product certification state, lineage completeness and dependency health.
Monitor identity and policy decision failures, denials, exceptional access, privilege changes and policy-version drift.
Monitor query and feature access, exports, unusual access patterns and masking or tokenisation failures using privacy-minimised telemetry.
Monitor dataset, metadata, backup, endpoint and key placement against declared jurisdiction policy.
Monitor retention actions, holds, deletion propagation, unresolved residues and evidence correlation.
Monitor audit producer sequence gaps, buffer health, integrity validation and evidence-access activity.
Test backup readability and controlled restore procedures; verify data, lineage and policy together before recording recovery success.
Maintain owner-routed alerts and runbooks for source failure, quality failure, lineage outage, identity outage, audit impairment, placement drift, deletion failure and regional recovery.
Review access entitlements, purpose assignments, source ownership, dataset ownership and privileged identities on a governed cadence that remains to be defined.

decisions.title: Use policy-selected regional deployment cells
decisions.selectedOption: Place ingestion, protected storage, processing, keys, token mappings, audit evidence and recovery copies in region-scoped cells selected from dataset and purpose policy.
alternatives: One global analytical store
Unrestricted cross-region replication
A separate fully isolated deployment for every dataset
decisions.rationale: SA-QR-002 requires enforceable placement and the supplied constraints state that policy varies by dataset and purpose. Region-scoped cells provide an explicit boundary while avoiding an unsupported assumption that one global location or unrestricted failover is valid. This candidate follows the AIW source-evidence-contract, conflict-detection and architecture-context-graph rules and is aligned with CAMBRIDGE-SA-1.0.
tradeoffs: Duplicates some regional operations and control deployment.
Makes cross-region analytics and recovery conditional on explicit policy.
Reduces the blast radius of a placement error but increases configuration-governance needs.
consequences: Every dataset requires a placement decision before intake.
Backups, metadata, audit evidence and token mappings require placement evaluation, not only analytical rows.
Regional failover is unavailable when policy does not permit another region.

decisions.title: Adopt coarse-grained governed services with explicit pipeline contracts
decisions.selectedOption: Decompose intake, ingestion, processing, catalog, access, privacy, lifecycle, audit and recovery into coarse-grained platform responsibilities with versioned stage contracts.
alternatives: Fine-grained microservices
A single undifferentiated application
Immediate federated data-mesh operating model
Uncontracted scripts and direct store access
decisions.rationale: The deterministic style analysis found Service-Based eligible but weak and found the other evaluated logical-application styles inapplicable or infeasible. The choice therefore uses coarse-grained boundaries as a reversible candidate without claiming an approved pattern. It also follows the AIW journey-grammar obligation for ownership, interface contracts and failure behaviour, with CAMBRIDGE-SA-1.0 as the approved knowledge reference.
tradeoffs: Coarse services may scale or release less independently than fine-grained services.
Explicit contracts add design and governance work.
Avoids the operational and security burden of unsupported fine-grained distribution.
consequences: Each service boundary requires an accountable owner, telemetry and failure semantics.
Boundary extraction remains possible if later evidence demonstrates independent scaling or release pressure.
No architecture pattern is considered accepted by this decision package.

decisions.title: Enforce role- and purpose-bound access through policy decisions
decisions.selectedOption: Use default-deny policy evaluation combining role, declared purpose, action, dataset, classification and jurisdiction, with obligations enforced at the common access gateway and analytical store.
alternatives: Role-based access alone
Direct consumer access to analytical tables
Manual ticket approval without runtime enforcement
Consumer-specific access logic
decisions.rationale: SA-FR-003 explicitly requires role and purpose binding, while varying jurisdiction policy makes static role grants insufficient. Central policy semantics with distributed enforcement provide a traceable decision for each access. This candidate is supported by the AIW requirements-taxonomy and architecture-context-graph rules and CAMBRIDGE-SA-1.0.
tradeoffs: Introduces dependency on governed identity attributes and policy availability.
Purpose vocabularies and policy administration require ownership.
Default denial can reduce availability during identity or policy faults.
consequences: Missing or indeterminate attributes are denied.
BI, model and export paths use the same policy vocabulary.
Policy version and decision correlation become mandatory audit fields.

decisions.title: Make lineage and product versioning publication gates
decisions.selectedOption: Represent every certified product with immutable input references, source checkpoints, transformation and configuration versions, quality results, classification and policy references; block publication if required lineage is incomplete.
alternatives: Best-effort lineage collected after publication
Table-level lineage without source checkpoints
Manual lineage documentation
Treat the analytical copy as the authoritative operational record
decisions.rationale: SA-FR-002 and SA-QR-004 require reproducibility and recovery without lineage loss, and SA-C-001 keeps source systems authoritative. Publication gating prevents a processed but untraceable output from appearing certified. This follows the AIW source-evidence-contract and requirements-taxonomy rules and CAMBRIDGE-SA-1.0.
tradeoffs: Lineage service impairment can delay publication.
Metadata volume and version management increase.
Rebuilds require source replay availability or retained source extracts.
consequences: Processing success and product publication are separate states.
The last certified product may remain available when a new version fails quality, subject to freshness policy.
Recovery validates lineage and source position before reopening access.

decisions.title: Apply classification-driven privacy transformations at trust boundaries
decisions.selectedOption: Classify direct and indirect identifiers and apply policy-selected minimisation, masking, tokenisation or denial before data enters a less-trusted processing or consumer context.
alternatives: Encrypt storage only
Mask all consumers identically
Rely on consumer-side handling
Remove all identifiers without considering analytical purpose
decisions.rationale: SA-QR-001 requires field protection across trust boundaries, and the scenario explicitly includes direct and indirect identifiers. A policy-selected transformation preserves necessary use while avoiding an unsupported single treatment for every field. This follows AIW conflict-detection and unsupported-metric-guard rules and CAMBRIDGE-SA-1.0.
tradeoffs: Tokenisation can retain linkage and therefore residual re-identification risk.
Irreversible transformation can reduce analytical utility.
Dynamic masking increases dependency on correct classification and policy.
consequences: No plaintext or unmasked fallback is permitted on privacy-control failure.
Reversible mappings are isolated and region constrained.
Derived products require classification reassessment rather than inheriting a weaker label automatically.

decisions.title: Treat required audit persistence as part of protected-action success
decisions.selectedOption: Correlate access, transformation, administration, export and lifecycle events in a segregated evidence service; block protected success when required evidence cannot be retained.
alternatives: Best-effort application logs
Retrospective reconstruction from platform logs
Permit actions during audit outage without durable evidence
Store full sensitive payloads in audit records
decisions.rationale: SA-FR-005 requires complete evidence. Best-effort logging cannot support a defensible claim of completeness, while full payload capture would create unnecessary sensitive copies. This follows the AIW source-evidence-contract and unsupported-metric-guard rules and CAMBRIDGE-SA-1.0.
tradeoffs: Audit impairment can reduce platform availability.
Durable regional buffering and sequence reconciliation add operational complexity.
Evidence minimisation may require correlated retrieval from multiple records.
consequences: Audit event schemas and correlation identifiers are governed contracts.
Evidence access is segregated from analytical access.
Gaps, buffering failures and integrity failures are operational alerts.

decisions.title: Coordinate retention, legal hold and deletion as a governed workflow
decisions.selectedOption: Use idempotent lifecycle actions across raw, derived, cached and controlled exported copies, with legal-hold precedence and explicit pending, blocked, complete or unresolved evidence.
alternatives: Delete only from the final analytical store
Rely on storage expiry without lineage-aware propagation
Perform manual deletion without correlated evidence
Allow retention expiry to override legal hold
decisions.rationale: SA-FR-004 requires retention, legal hold and defensible deletion. A lineage-aware workflow is needed because derived products and caches can preserve information after a primary copy is removed. This candidate follows AIW requirements-taxonomy and architecture-context-graph rules and CAMBRIDGE-SA-1.0.
tradeoffs: Deletion propagation is more complex across derived products and exports.
Legal hold can delay deletion and increase retained volume.
Downstream copies outside platform control require contractual evidence or remain unresolved.
consequences: A deletion is not complete while an in-scope residue is unresolved.
Hold release and deletion require privileged, audited actions.
Retention schedules and hold authorities must be supplied before implementation acceptance.

decisions.title: Recover data, lineage and access policy as one product
decisions.selectedOption: Restore a versioned product bundle in a permitted region and validate source checkpoint, lineage, classification, policy, key references and audit correlation before reopening consumption.
alternatives: Restore analytical data only
Rebuild policy manually after data restoration
Fail over automatically to any available region
Use source replay without preserving transformation versions
decisions.rationale: SA-QR-004 explicitly requires recovery without losing source lineage or access policy. The deterministic finding also requires a recovery decision covering backup, failover and testing. This candidate records that decision without claiming acceptance and is aligned with CAMBRIDGE-SA-1.0.
tradeoffs: Coordinated recovery is slower and more complex than restoring data alone.
Recovery remains unavailable where no policy-permitted target exists.
Validation can prolong consumer unavailability but prevents uncontrolled reopening.
consequences: Backups include metadata and policy references needed for validation.
Recovery exercises test access denial and lineage as well as data readability.
Dataset recovery objectives remain unresolved and require human approval.

decisions.title: Apply placement and classification policy to metadata and control artifacts
decisions.selectedOption: Classify lineage, catalog entries, audit evidence, backups, token mappings and operational metadata, and keep them regional when they can reveal or reconstruct restricted information.
alternatives: Treat all metadata as globally unrestricted
Keep data regional but centralise all audit and lineage records
Duplicate metadata to every region
Remove metadata needed for recovery
decisions.rationale: The residency requirement applies to information risk, not only analytical table rows. Metadata and token mappings can expose identifiers, relationships or locations. This is a conservative candidate derived from SA-QR-001 and SA-QR-002 under the AIW source-evidence-contract rule and CAMBRIDGE-SA-1.0.
tradeoffs: Regional metadata partitioning complicates global discovery and assurance.
Auditors may need federated evidence retrieval.
Over-classification can reduce operational visibility.
consequences: Global metadata replication requires explicit policy evaluation.
Operational telemetry must minimise sensitive labels and values.
Recovery planning includes region-local metadata and evidence.

risks.description: Direct identifiers, indirect identifiers or derived features may enable re-identification despite masking or tokenisation.
risks.mitigation: Classify inputs and derived products, minimise fields, test transformations against approved use, isolate reversible mappings and reassess risk before new consumer purposes or exports.

risks.description: Data, metadata, backups, audit evidence or token mappings may be stored or processed in an unauthorised jurisdiction.
risks.mitigation: Use dataset- and purpose-specific placement policy, region-scoped endpoints and keys, deployment-policy checks, movement denial and placement-drift monitoring.
risks.owner: Data owner with Privacy officer oversight

risks.description: Privilege or purpose assignments may accumulate, become stale or permit broader use than intended.
risks.mitigation: Default deny, separate administrative duties, time- and scope-bound grants, periodic entitlement review, policy-change audit and exceptional-access review.

risks.description: Lineage may be incomplete, inconsistent with stored data or lost during transformation and recovery.
risks.mitigation: Gate publication on lineage persistence, use stable product and input identities, version transformations, reconcile catalog and store state and include lineage in recovery tests.

risks.description: Stale or poor-quality data may be consumed as if current and certified.
risks.mitigation: Make freshness and certification explicit, quarantine failures, retain the last certified version without silent substitution, alert owners and expose classified consumer failures.

risks.description: Audit-event loss, tampering or excessive sensitive payload capture may make evidence incomplete or create a new disclosure risk.
risks.mitigation: Use authenticated producers, append-only permissions, integrity and sequence checks, regional buffering, evidence minimisation, gap alerts and fail-closed protected actions.

risks.description: Deletion may be reported complete while derived, cached, backup or exported copies remain, or deletion may violate an active hold.
risks.mitigation: Use lineage-aware idempotent propagation, hold precedence, residue tracking, backup lifecycle controls and explicit unresolved outcomes rather than false completion.
risks.owner: Data owner with Privacy officer oversight

risks.description: Identity or policy dependency failure may cause excessive denial or tempt operators to bypass purpose-bound controls.
risks.mitigation: Fail closed, prohibit inferred attributes and manual data-plane bypass, monitor dependency health and maintain a governed exceptional-access process if one is later approved.

risks.description: Source contract drift, weak ordering semantics or insufficient replay history may prevent reproducible ingestion and rebuild.
risks.mitigation: Version source contracts, validate schemas, preserve checkpoints, quarantine incompatible changes and obtain source-owner agreement for ordering, replay and late-arrival semantics.

risks.description: The duplicate requirements, inconsistent deterministic journey and compatibility graph projection may create incorrect architecture lineage if treated as accepted context.
risks.mitigation: Human-adjudicate REQ-001 and REQ-002, replace the mismatched journey and context participants, then materialise a canonical graph through governed approval.

risks.description: Recovery may restore data into an impermissible region or reopen a product with stale classification or access policy.
risks.mitigation: Authorise the target region per dataset, restore metadata and policy references with data, validate denial and lineage behavior and keep failed restores closed.

delivery.executiveSummary: This candidate architecture uses region-scoped data planes, coarse-grained governed services, publication-gated lineage, role- and purpose-bound policy enforcement, classification-driven privacy controls, lifecycle orchestration and correlated audit evidence. Protected operations fail closed when identity, policy, privacy or required audit controls are indeterminate. Recovery treats data, lineage, classification and access policy as one product and never assumes unrestricted cross-region failover. The package is not production-accepted: jurisdiction matrices, purpose governance, retention and hold rules, recovery objectives, source replay contracts and export obligations remain unresolved. The duplicate requirement, inconsistent deterministic journey and compatibility Design Graph projection also require human adjudication. AIW rules support the ownership, failure-semantics, traceability and unsupported-metric posture, while CAMBRIDGE-SA-1.0 is the only cited knowledge reference.

sddSections.heading: 1. Status and architecture intent
sddSections.content: Candidate-only solution architecture for BIA1-S3. It covers governed ingestion, transformation, BI and model consumption, privacy, residency, lineage, lifecycle, audit and recovery. It does not approve a pattern, ADR, deployment or canonical graph.

sddSections.heading: 2. Logical architecture
sddSections.content: The platform is decomposed into source intake, regional ingestion, protected landing, transformation and quality, catalog and lineage, policy, analytical storage, access gateway, privacy protection, lifecycle, audit and operations/recovery responsibilities. Interfaces are versioned and have named owners and explicit failure semantics.

sddSections.heading: 3. Data and lineage
sddSections.content: Every product is linked to its source owner, source checkpoint or extract, input versions, transformation and configuration versions, quality result, classification and policy references. Publication is blocked when required lineage is incomplete. Source systems remain authoritative.

sddSections.heading: 4. Security and privacy
sddSections.content: Access is denied by default and combines role, declared purpose, action, classification and jurisdiction. Trust-boundary crossings apply encryption and policy-selected masking, tokenisation, minimisation or denial. Keys and reversible mappings are isolated and region constrained.

sddSections.heading: 5. Residency and deployment
sddSections.content: Data-plane components are deployed in region-scoped cells selected from dataset and purpose policy. Metadata, backups, audit evidence and token mappings receive their own placement classification. Cross-region movement and failover require explicit policy permission.

sddSections.heading: 6. Lifecycle management
sddSections.content: Retention, legal hold and deletion are coordinated across protected landing, certified products, caches and controlled exports. Legal hold blocks deletion. Partial propagation remains unresolved and auditable rather than being reported as successful.

sddSections.heading: 7. Audit and evidence
sddSections.content: Access, policy, transformation, administrative, export and lifecycle events are correlated in a segregated evidence service. Required evidence persistence is part of protected-action success. Evidence payloads are minimised to avoid creating another sensitive-data store.

sddSections.heading: 8. Resilience and recovery
sddSections.content: Source, quality, lineage, identity, privacy, audit, lifecycle and regional failures have explicit fail-closed or quarantine paths. Recovery restores data with lineage, classification, policy and audit references in an allowed region and validates them before reopening access.

sddSections.heading: 9. Operations
sddSections.content: Operations monitor checkpoints, quality, certification, lineage, policy decisions, exports, placement drift, audit gaps, lifecycle residues and restore validation. Alerts route to source owners, stewards, Security, Privacy or SRE according to responsibility.

sddSections.heading: 10. Governance basis
sddSections.content: The design applies the AIW source-evidence-contract, requirements-taxonomy, conflict-detection, journey-grammar, architecture-context-graph and unsupported-metric-guard rules. The deterministic recovery finding is addressed by proposed decision D-08. CAMBRIDGE-SA-1.0 is the approved knowledge reference. Human approval remains mandatory.
