acceptanceAndFitnessTests: Attempt source onboarding without a source owner, classification or jurisdiction policy; intake must be rejected with a classified and auditable failure.
Replay a previously accepted batch or CDC position; processing must be idempotent and must not create an uncorrelated duplicate product.
Introduce an incompatible schema change; the feed must be quarantined and its durable checkpoint must not advance.
Cause a required data-quality rule to fail; the candidate product must remain uncertified and unavailable while the last certified version is not silently relabelled.
Remove required lineage metadata during publication; product publication must fail even if transformation output exists.
Test an access matrix across role, purpose, action, classification and region; unauthorised, missing and indeterminate combinations must be denied and audited.
Request the same dataset through BI and model paths; both must apply the common policy vocabulary, regional controls and required privacy obligations.
Cause the masking, tokenisation or key service to fail; no unmasked or plaintext fallback may be returned.
Attempt a cross-region write, backup, metadata replication or restore not permitted by dataset policy; the action must be blocked and evidenced.
Make the audit service unavailable and exhaust the permitted evidence path; protected publication, access, export and lifecycle success must stop.
Apply a deletion while a legal hold is active; deletion must be blocked and the hold decision must be auditable.
Inject a partial deletion failure; completion must remain unresolved until every in-scope copy succeeds or an authorised exception is recorded.
Restore a product without its required lineage or policy version; the restored product must remain closed to consumers.
Restore a complete product bundle in a permitted region; source references, lineage, classification, access denial and audit correlation must be validated before reopening.
Verify that analytical records identify their authoritative source and that no operational write-back or system-of-record claim is exposed.
Attempt catalog discovery for an unauthorised dataset; sensitive metadata must not be returned and direct-store discovery must not bypass the catalog policy.
Review privileged policy, classification, key, hold, deletion and recovery changes; each must identify the authorised actor, outcome and correlation evidence.
Confirm that logs, traces, quarantine diagnostics and audit events do not contain unnecessary sensitive payloads, keys or reversible token mappings.

abstentions: No recovery time, recovery point, availability, freshness, throughput, retention duration or audit-storage metric was invented.
No jurisdiction-specific law, regulatory obligation or legal interpretation was asserted because none was supplied.
No cloud provider, database, catalog, identity, cryptographic or observability product was selected.
No masking or tokenisation method was declared sufficient for every identifier or analytical purpose.
No architecture style, pattern, ADR, Design Graph record or production deployment was approved.
No sensitive value, redacted attribute or missing identity field was inferred or reconstructed.
No cross-region failover permission was assumed.
No deterministic readiness score was converted into an approval claim.
unsupportedClaimsRejected: The architecture review readiness score does not establish production acceptance.
The compatibility Design Graph projection is not a canonical architect-approved graph.
The proposed review ADR and decisions are not accepted records.
Pattern evidence mentioned by the review does not mean a governed pattern has been selected.
A global store or unrestricted replication cannot be justified without the missing jurisdiction matrix.
Complete auditability cannot be claimed until event coverage, retention, integrity and failure tests are accepted.
Defensible deletion cannot be claimed until downstream copies, backups, exports and legal-hold rules are defined and tested.
Recoverability cannot be claimed from data backup alone because lineage, classification and access policy also require validation.

problemUnderstanding.businessObjective: Modernise the legacy core-banking estate through governed, cohort-based coexistence and migration while preserving customer access, financial authority, regulatory reporting, operational control and reversible transition states.
scope: Preserve channel access across legacy and target cores.
Route account and product activity according to governed migration state.
Migrate customer, account, product, balance and transaction data in dependency-aware waves.
Integrate product processing with payments, the general ledger and regulatory reporting.
Reconcile business data and financial postings around every wave.
Control cutover, rollback, forward recovery and exceptions.
Migrate batch and end-of-day dependencies.
Provide security, audit, operational telemetry and customer-support controls across both estates.
journeys: A customer invokes an account, payment or product capability; coexistence routing resolves migration state and sends the request to exactly one authoritative core or returns a classified failure.
Product processing produces controlled payment, ledger and regulatory outcomes with correlation and reconciliation evidence.
The migration office prepares a dependency-closed cohort, copies and validates data, rehearses cutover, changes governed routing state and verifies the outcome.
Operations detect a failed or indeterminate cutover and invoke rollback or forward recovery from an evidenced checkpoint.
Batch and end-of-day workloads execute under a dependency schedule spanning both cores, with explicit cut-off, retry and exception handling.
Finance and regulatory reporting reconcile source transactions, balances, ledger postings and reporting extracts before a wave is closed.
Customer support uses correlated status and exception evidence without directly changing core records or migration state.

qualityDrivers.statement: Customer-facing capabilities must remain observable and controlled throughout each transition state, with transition service-level indicators and acceptance thresholds defined before a migration wave.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Derived from CB-QR-001; numeric thresholds are not supplied and must not be invented.

qualityDrivers.statement: Authentication, authorization, auditability and segregation of duties must span channels, migration controls, both cores and financial integrations.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Derived from CB-QR-002 and the authoritative nature of financial and regulatory processing.

qualityDrivers.statement: Migration, cutover and recovery must use rehearsed checkpoints, classified failure paths and evidence-based release gates.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Derived from CB-QR-003, CB-FR-005 and the deterministic GOV-RECOVERY-DECISION advisory.

qualityDrivers.statement: Technical health and business reconciliation must be correlated across both estates, batch processing, ledger posting and reporting.
qualityDrivers.rationale: Derived from CB-QR-004 and CB-FR-004.

constraints: CB-C-001: The legacy core cannot be replaced in a single big-bang event.
CB-C-002: Regulatory and general-ledger obligations remain authoritative throughout transition.
Legacy interfaces and batch windows have incomplete documentation.
Customer and account migration ordering is constrained by product dependencies.
The candidate Design Graph is a compatibility projection and has not been materialized or approved.
assumptions: A migration control plane can hold account-level migration state.
Parallel reconciliation can compare legacy and target outcomes.
Stable business identifiers and correlation identifiers can be established across both estates; this requires validation.
Legacy and target interfaces can expose sufficient data for migration and reconciliation; this requires discovery.
Rollback is possible only before an explicitly defined point of no return; externally committed effects may require forward recovery.
ambiguities: The authoritative system of record for each entity and transition state has not been agreed.
Legacy API, file, batch-window and end-of-day dependency inventories are incomplete.
Product dependency rules and therefore the exact migration cohort order are unknown.
Transaction boundaries across core processing, payment rails, ledger posting and reporting are unspecified.
Transition service-level indicators are identifiable, but their thresholds and measurement windows are not supplied.
The point of no return and compensating actions for externally committed payment or ledger effects are unspecified.
Retention, classification and access requirements for migration and reconciliation evidence are unspecified.
Recovery objectives, backup coverage and failover ownership are not supplied.
unresolvedQuestions: Which system is authoritative for Customer, Account, Product, Balance, Transaction and Ledger data in every migration state?
What dependency graph determines valid customer, account and product cohorts?
Which legacy interfaces and batch jobs are required by each customer journey and financial close process?
What transition service-level thresholds must gate cutover, rollback and wave closure?
Which payment, ledger or reporting effects are reversible, compensatable or forward-recovery-only?
What recovery objectives and backup validation criteria apply to the routing state, evidence store, target core and integration components?
Who has maker, checker and emergency authority for migration-state transitions?
What reconciliation differences are tolerable, explainable or blocking for each data class?

systemContext: Customers and customer-support users access customer, account, payment and product capabilities through existing Channels.
A coexistence boundary mediates access to Legacy Core and Target Core using governed account-level migration state.
Product and core outcomes integrate with Payment Rails, General Ledger and Regulatory Reporting through controlled adapters.
The Migration Office operates data migration, cutover and rollback workflows; it does not bypass routing-state governance.
Operations and SRE observe technical health, batch execution and business reconciliation across both estates.
Finance and Regulatory Reporting retain authority over ledger and reporting acceptance throughout transition.
Security and Risk govern privileged access, segregation of duties and audit evidence.
The candidate context is consistent with the AIW architecture-context-graph and journey-grammar rules, but remains unapproved.

components.description: Existing channel-facing API boundary retained during coexistence.
components.responsibility: Preserve stable customer-facing contracts, authenticate callers, propagate correlation identifiers and return classified outcomes without exposing core selection.

components.name: Coexistence Router
components.description: Coarse-grained routing service between channels and the two core estates.
components.responsibility: Resolve governed migration state and route each eligible operation to one authoritative core; reject ambiguous or unavailable routing decisions rather than guessing.

components.name: Migration Control Plane
components.description: Governed store and workflow for account-level migration state.
components.responsibility: Maintain versioned migration state, permitted transitions, cohort membership, approvals, checkpoints and an auditable history under segregation of duties.

components.name: Legacy Core Facade
components.description: Anti-corruption boundary around legacy online and batch interfaces.
components.responsibility: Translate canonical requests to documented legacy contracts, normalize outcomes and isolate channels from legacy-specific semantics.

components.name: Target Core Facade
components.description: Controlled boundary around target-core online and batch capabilities.
components.responsibility: Translate canonical requests to target-core contracts, enforce idempotency and correlation expectations, and normalize outcomes for coexistence.

components.name: Payments, Ledger and Reporting Integration
components.description: Controlled integration boundary for payment rails, general-ledger posting and regulatory extracts.
components.responsibility: Validate, correlate and deliver financial outcomes to authoritative external destinations while recording accepted, rejected and indeterminate states for reconciliation.

components.name: Reconciliation and Evidence Service
components.description: Independent comparison and evidence capability spanning both estates and financial destinations.
components.responsibility: Compare source counts, business entities, balances, transactions, postings and extracts; classify differences and produce tamper-evident wave evidence.

components.name: Migration Data Pipeline
components.description: Restartable pipeline for extraction, transformation, validation and loading.
components.responsibility: Move dependency-closed data cohorts from legacy to target using checkpoints, lineage, validation and quarantined exception handling without changing authority by itself.

components.name: Cutover Orchestrator
components.description: Runbook-driven coordinator for rehearsals, cutover, rollback and forward recovery.
components.responsibility: Execute approved transition steps, enforce gates, preserve checkpoints, coordinate routing changes and stop on unresolved reconciliation or dependency failures.

components.name: Batch and End-of-Day Coordinator
components.description: Control boundary for existing scheduler dependencies and migrated batch workloads.
components.responsibility: Model dependencies, cut-offs, retries and ownership across both cores, preventing wave closure when required end-of-day outcomes are incomplete or indeterminate.

components.name: Operations and Observability Plane
components.description: Cross-estate operational telemetry, alerting and runbook entry point.
components.responsibility: Correlate channel, routing, core, integration, batch and reconciliation health while separating technical symptoms from business-integrity exceptions.

components.name: Exception and Support Workbench
components.description: Role-restricted view of customer-impacting and migration exceptions.
components.responsibility: Expose correlated status, evidence and approved next actions to Operations and Customer Support without permitting direct mutation of core balances or uncontrolled migration-state changes.

components.name: Security and Audit Controls
components.description: Cross-cutting identity, authorization, secrets and audit controls.
components.responsibility: Enforce least privilege, privileged-operation approval, service authentication, protected secrets and tamper-evident audit events across coexistence.

interfaces.name: Channel Capability API
interfaces.contract: Versioned customer, account, payment and product operations with authenticated identity, correlation identifier and normalized success, rejection or indeterminate outcome.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: No core selection is accepted from the caller. Timeouts or malformed requests return a classified failure; retries require operation-specific idempotency and retain the original correlation identifier.

interfaces.name: Migration-State Resolution API
interfaces.contract: Read account-level state, version, cohort and permitted routing action; mutate state only through approved orchestration commands.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: A stale, missing, conflicting or unavailable state fails closed before core invocation. Version checks prevent lost updates; no default core is guessed.

interfaces.name: Legacy Core Canonical API
interfaces.contract: Canonical customer, account, payment and product operations translated to legacy contracts with stable error taxonomy and correlation.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Only invoked when legacy is authoritative. Retries are bounded by the operation's idempotency classification; indeterminate writes are quarantined for status inquiry and reconciliation rather than sent to the target core.

interfaces.name: Target Core Canonical API
interfaces.contract: Canonical customer, account, payment and product operations translated to target-core contracts with idempotency key and correlation propagation.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Only invoked when target is authoritative. Duplicate keys return the prior known outcome; indeterminate writes trigger status inquiry and reconciliation, not legacy replay.

interfaces.name: Core Financial Outcome Contract
interfaces.source: CMP-04 Legacy Core Facade and CMP-05 Target Core Facade
interfaces.target: CMP-06 Payments, Ledger and Reporting Integration
interfaces.contract: Correlated transaction, payment, posting and reporting outcomes identify source core, account, migration state, business date and processing status.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: The integration boundary deduplicates by governed business key. Accepted, rejected and indeterminate outcomes are persisted for reconciliation; an indeterminate external effect blocks blind resubmission.

interfaces.name: Payment Rail Interface
interfaces.source: CMP-06 Payments, Ledger and Reporting Integration
interfaces.contract: Existing payment-rail contract wrapped with canonical correlation, status inquiry and exception classification.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: External acceptance is treated as an irreversible or compensatable effect according to the rail contract. Timeout after submission is indeterminate and requires inquiry before retry or recovery.

interfaces.name: General-Ledger Posting Interface
interfaces.source: CMP-06 Payments, Ledger and Reporting Integration
interfaces.contract: Balanced, correlated posting instructions and acknowledgements identifying business date, source core and migration wave.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: The general ledger remains authoritative for accepted postings. Rejected or indeterminate postings enter an owned exception queue; duplicates are detected by governed posting identity.

interfaces.name: Regulatory Extract Interface
interfaces.source: CMP-06 Payments, Ledger and Reporting Integration
interfaces.contract: Versioned extract or feed containing lineage to source transactions, balances, ledger outcomes and migration wave.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: An incomplete, duplicate or unreconciled extract is quarantined and cannot be marked accepted. Correction and resubmission follow the reporting owner's existing authority.

interfaces.name: Migration Data Transfer Contract
interfaces.owner: Migration office with Data and Target Core owners
interfaces.contract: Versioned cohort extracts, transformations, validation results, lineage, checkpoint and load outcome.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Loads are restartable from checkpoints and idempotent by entity version or migration key. Invalid records are quarantined; pipeline completion never changes routing authority automatically.

interfaces.name: Reconciliation Evidence Feed
interfaces.source: Legacy Core, Target Core, General Ledger and Regulatory Reporting
interfaces.contract: Comparable snapshots or outcome feeds for customers, accounts, products, balances, transactions, postings and extracts with common identifiers and business cut-offs.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Late or missing feeds produce an incomplete result rather than an inferred match. Unexplained differences block the associated migration gate until resolved or explicitly dispositioned by an authorized owner.

interfaces.name: Cutover Command Interface
interfaces.target: CMP-03 Migration Control Plane and CMP-02 Coexistence Router
interfaces.contract: Approved prepare, cutover, rollback, forward-recovery and close commands carrying cohort, expected state version, checkpoint and approval evidence.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Commands are idempotent and compare expected versions. Partial execution stops the workflow and records actual state; automated progression is prohibited when a gate is failed or indeterminate.

interfaces.name: Batch Control Interface
interfaces.contract: Dependency-aware job start, completion, cut-off, retry, cancellation and exception status across legacy, target, ledger and reporting jobs.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: A missing prerequisite, overrun or indeterminate completion prevents dependent jobs and wave closure. Retries resume from an evidenced checkpoint or invoke an approved recovery runbook.

interfaces.name: Cross-Estate Telemetry Contract
interfaces.contract: Structured health, dependency, business-event and reconciliation telemetry carrying component, cohort, migration state and correlation identifiers without exposed sensitive payloads.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Telemetry loss raises an observability impairment and can block cutover where required evidence is unavailable; it does not change transaction outcomes or migration state.

interfaces.name: Support Exception Interface
interfaces.target: CMP-07 Reconciliation and Evidence Service and CMP-09 Cutover Orchestrator
interfaces.contract: Read correlated status and evidence, create an exception case and request an approved operational action.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: The workbench cannot directly edit balances, postings or routing state. Stale or incomplete evidence is displayed as indeterminate and escalated rather than represented as success.

interfaces.name: Security and Audit Event Interface
interfaces.contract: Identity, authorization decision, privileged command, configuration change and evidence-access events with correlation and actor context.
interfaces.consistencyAndFailureSemantics: Security-control failure denies privileged state change. Audit-delivery failure is surfaced and queued through a protected path; it cannot be silently discarded.

dataArchitecture: Define an explicit authority matrix for Customer, Account, Product, Balance, Transaction, Ledger, Migration State and Reconciliation Evidence in each transition state; this matrix is an unresolved implementation gate.
Use stable business identifiers, source-system identifiers, entity versions, business date, migration-wave identifier and end-to-end correlation identifiers.
Maintain a single active processing authority per account and operation. Do not implement uncontrolled application-level dual writes to both cores.
The Migration Control Plane owns migration state and its transition history; core business data remains owned by the authoritative core for the current state.
Migration extracts are immutable by version, lineage-bearing and restartable. Transformation rules and validation results are retained with each cohort.
Reconciliation independently compares legacy, target, payment, ledger and reporting outcomes. Missing evidence is incomplete, not successful.
Classify differences as expected transformation, timing, duplicate, missing, value mismatch or unresolved; only authorized owners may disposition them.
Protect migration and reconciliation data according to an agreed classification and retention schedule; those details remain open.
Use checkpoints before data copy, final delta, routing change, batch close and wave closure. Externally committed effects are separately tracked for compensation or forward recovery.
securityArchitecture: Apply least privilege to channels, services, bulk migration, support, operations and evidence access.
Separate migration preparation, state-change request, approval and execution roles; define emergency access with retrospective audit.
Authenticate service-to-service calls and protect data in transit using capabilities supported by each estate.
Protect credentials and cryptographic material outside application configuration and rotate them through an owned operational process.
Record identity, authorization, migration-state transition, cutover command, reconciliation disposition, posting and evidence-access events in tamper-evident audit history.
Mask or omit sensitive customer and financial values from logs, metrics and support views.
Restrict bulk extraction and migration access by cohort, purpose and duration.
Threat-model ambiguous routing, replay, duplicate posting, privileged misuse, evidence tampering and migration-data exfiltration before the first authority-changing wave.
deploymentRuntime: Run the legacy and target cores concurrently for the coexistence period; no big-bang replacement is assumed.
Deploy routing, migration control, reconciliation, orchestration, observability and security controls independently of either core's failure domain where the available estate permits.
Separate customer transaction paths from bulk migration and reconciliation workloads so migration activity cannot silently consume all operational capacity.
Use controlled configuration and release promotion for routing rules, canonical contracts, transformation rules and batch dependencies.
Provide redundant runtime instances and protected state for critical coexistence components only after recovery objectives and topology are agreed; no quantitative availability claim is made.
Keep non-production rehearsal environments representative enough to exercise interfaces, batch dependencies, cutover and recovery without using uncontrolled production data.
Maintain a runtime inventory mapping component, owner, dependency, configuration version, runbook and telemetry source across both estates.
resilienceFailurePaths: Migration-state lookup unavailable or ambiguous: fail closed before invoking a core, preserve correlation, notify Operations and do not guess a default route.
Core request times out before a known outcome: perform status inquiry using the original idempotency and correlation keys; quarantine unresolved writes and prohibit replay to the other core.
Payment, ledger or reporting submission is indeterminate: stop blind retries, query destination status and reconcile before compensation, resubmission or forward recovery.
Data-copy validation fails: quarantine the affected records, leave legacy authority unchanged and prevent cohort cutover.
Pre-cutover reconciliation fails: stop the wave, preserve checkpoints and assign exceptions to Finance, Migration or Product owners.
Routing changes partially: halt orchestration, compare actual state versions and restore the last evidenced safe state where no irreversible external effect has occurred.

Post-cutover customer or integrity failure occurs before the point of no return: stop new target routing, drain or classify in-flight work, restore data and state from the checkpoint, reconcile, then return authority to legacy.
Failure occurs after irreversible payment or ledger effects: do not perform blind rollback; isolate the cohort and execute an approved forward-recovery or compensation plan.
Batch prerequisite is missing or a job overruns: prevent dependent end-of-day steps, retain the current business cut-off state and invoke the owned recovery runbook.
Reconciliation or telemetry evidence is unavailable: mark the gate indeterminate and prevent wave closure.
Security or audit control fails for a privileged command: deny the command and raise a security incident path.
Recovery strategy remains candidate until an ADR defines backup scope, failover ownership, recovery objectives and rehearsal evidence, as required by deterministic finding GOV-RECOVERY-DECISION.
observabilityOperations: Correlate customer operation, account, migration state, selected core, payment, ledger posting, regulatory extract, batch run and reconciliation result without exposing sensitive payloads.
Measure channel success and classified failure, dependency health, routing-state errors, indeterminate outcomes, duplicate detection, batch completion, reconciliation exceptions and support cases.
Define transition service-level thresholds and measurement windows with business and operational owners before each authority-changing wave; none are supplied in the scenario.
Provide separate dashboards for customer service, technical health, financial reconciliation, batch progress and migration-wave gates.
Alert on ambiguous routing, unknown transaction outcomes, unreconciled postings, incomplete extracts, batch dependency failures, privileged state changes and audit-delivery failure.
Maintain runbooks for state-store failure, core timeout, duplicate posting, reconciliation mismatch, failed cutover, batch overrun and security-control failure.
Record owner, acknowledgement, action and final disposition for every migration-blocking exception.
Review operational evidence after each rehearsal and wave before expanding the next cohort.
transitionArchitecture: TA-0 Discovery and baseline: inventory channel, payment, ledger, reporting and batch contracts; build the product dependency graph; establish current service and reconciliation baselines.
TA-1 Controlled façade: place canonical channel and financial contracts around legacy behavior without moving authority; validate correlation, error taxonomy, audit and observability.

TA-2 Shadow migration: copy a dependency-closed cohort to the target while legacy remains authoritative; run target processing only where it cannot create uncontrolled external effects and compare outcomes.
TA-3 Cohort coexistence: after approved rehearsal and reconciliation gates, change governed account state so the target becomes authoritative for the cohort while other cohorts remain on legacy.
TA-4 Target consolidation: migrate remaining dependency-closed cohorts, including batch and end-of-day ownership, while maintaining exceptions as explicitly governed states.

TA-5 Legacy retirement candidate: remove a legacy capability only after no routed cohort or batch dependency requires it and financial, regulatory, recovery and retention evidence is accepted by authorized humans.
Wave 0 establishes controls, canonical contracts, discovery evidence and cutover rehearsal without transferring customer authority.
Subsequent waves are selected from the validated product dependency graph; the exact order is intentionally unresolved rather than assuming low-risk cohorts.
Each wave has entry gates for dependency completeness, data validation, security controls, runbook rehearsal, capacity evidence and agreed service-level thresholds.

Each cutover captures a checkpoint, stops conflicting migration changes, drains or classifies in-flight work, applies final delta, reconciles, changes versioned routing state and verifies customer, batch and financial outcomes.
Rollback restores legacy authority only when the data checkpoint can be restored and no unresolved irreversible external effect exists; otherwise the workflow enters forward recovery.
Long-tail exceptions remain isolated and explicitly owned rather than being forced into a nominal wave or silently dual-processed.

decisions.title: Use coarse-grained service-based coexistence boundaries
decisions.selectedOption: Candidate selection: a small set of coarse-grained services for routing, migration control, financial integration, reconciliation and operations, evolving boundaries only when evidence justifies further distribution.
alternatives: Direct channel integration with both cores
Fine-grained microservices
Event-driven architecture as the primary application style
Single deployable modular monolith
decisions.rationale: The AIW deterministic recommendation identifies Service-Based as the only eligible logical-application style, although feasibility is weak. CAMBRIDGE-SA-1.0 and the deterministic context favor reversible, coarse-grained evolution for regulated financial modernization while warning about distributed security and operating burden.
tradeoffs: Adds coexistence components and operational dependencies.
Limits independent deployment compared with fine-grained microservices.
Reduces channel coupling to either core and supports staged replacement.
consequences: Service ownership, monitoring, failure handling and rollback preconditions must be documented.
Further distribution requires operational evidence and a reviewed ADR.
This selection remains candidate and does not accept a governed pattern record.

decisions.title: Route by versioned account-level migration state
decisions.selectedOption: The Migration Control Plane owns versioned account-level state; the Coexistence Router invokes exactly one authoritative core for each eligible operation.
alternatives: Channel-specific routing rules
Static product-level routing
Dual processing in both cores
Target-first routing with fallback to legacy
decisions.rationale: CB-FR-003 explicitly requires governed migration-state routing, and the supplied assumption permits account-level state. Failing closed avoids unsupported inference when state is unavailable.
tradeoffs: Introduces a critical state dependency.
Account-level control increases state volume and operational discipline.
Prevents transparent fallback after an indeterminate write.
consequences: State transitions require explicit approvals and optimistic version checks.
State availability and recovery require a dedicated ADR and tests.
No caller may select the core directly.

decisions.title: Use canonical contracts and anti-corruption facades
decisions.selectedOption: Preserve stable channel and financial contracts while isolating legacy and target semantics behind separate facades.
alternatives: Expose native core contracts to every channel
Create a single shared adapter for both cores
Rewrite all consuming channels before migration
decisions.rationale: Incomplete legacy documentation and coexistence make core-specific coupling unsafe. The source-evidence-contract rule supports explicit contracts and traceable boundaries rather than assumed equivalence.
tradeoffs: Requires translation and semantic mapping.
Can hide core differences unless contract tests are comprehensive.
Reduces repeated migration changes in channels and external integrations.
consequences: Every mapped field and error requires lineage and contract tests.
Core-specific capabilities must not leak into shared contracts without review.
Adapter failure semantics and owners are explicit.

decisions.title: Make independent reconciliation a migration gate
decisions.selectedOption: Use an independent service to compare data, transaction, balance, ledger and reporting outcomes before cutover, after cutover and before wave closure.
alternatives: Rely on target-core validation only
Perform finance reconciliation after all waves
Compare record counts without financial outcomes
decisions.rationale: CB-FR-004 and CB-C-002 require continuing financial authority. The deterministically derived reconciliation journey requires immutable evidence, exception workflow, cut-off and retry policy.
tradeoffs: Adds data extraction and storage overhead.
Timing differences can create false exceptions without agreed cut-offs.
Provides auditable evidence and earlier divergence detection.
consequences: Unexplained or incomplete results block the associated gate.
Finance and Regulatory Reporting own acceptance of their outcomes.
Tolerance rules must be explicitly approved rather than inferred.

decisions.title: Use an explicit reversible transition state machine
decisions.selectedOption: Candidate states are LEGACY_AUTHORITY, COPY_IN_PROGRESS, SHADOW_VALIDATION, CUTOVER_PENDING, TARGET_AUTHORITY, ROLLBACK_PENDING and EXCEPTION, with only approved transitions.
alternatives: Binary migrated flag
Manual routing configuration changes
Time-based automatic cutover
Always-on dual processing
decisions.rationale: The objective requires reversible transition states, while CB-FR-005 requires controlled rollback and exception handling. Explicit states preserve uncertainty and prevent implicit progression.
tradeoffs: More operational states and runbooks must be maintained.
Rollback eligibility depends on data and external-effect checkpoints.
Provides clear ownership and auditable recovery paths.
consequences: No automatic promotion occurs between states.
Each transition records expected version, approvals, checkpoint and result.
Post-point-of-no-return failures use forward recovery rather than assumed rollback.

decisions.title: Migrate batch and end-of-day work by dependency graph
decisions.selectedOption: Inventory jobs and cut-offs, model dependencies across both cores and move dependency-closed batch groups under a common coordinator.
alternatives: Move all batch after online migration
Retain all batch on legacy indefinitely
Duplicate complete end-of-day processing in both cores
decisions.rationale: CB-FR-006 requires retained operational control, and the scenario states that documentation and migration ordering are incomplete.
tradeoffs: Discovery may delay authority-changing waves.
Temporary cross-estate dependencies remain.
Controlled sequencing reduces hidden end-of-day failure.
consequences: Unknown dependencies are migration blockers, not assumptions.
Every job requires owner, input, output, cut-off, retry and recovery semantics.
Wave closure includes batch and financial-close evidence.

decisions.title: Apply cross-estate least privilege, segregation and tamper-evident audit
decisions.selectedOption: Use named human and service identities, least-privilege authorization, maker-checker migration commands and tamper-evident audit correlation across both estates.
alternatives: Retain separate uncorrelated legacy and target controls
Permit migration operators direct core access
Rely on application logs as the sole audit record
decisions.rationale: CB-QR-002 requires security, auditability and segregation of duties throughout coexistence. CAMBRIDGE-SA-1.0 supports explicit control ownership and evidence obligations.
tradeoffs: Adds identity integration and privileged-workflow overhead.
Legacy control limitations may require compensating procedures.
Improves traceability of high-impact actions.
consequences: The detailed role matrix remains to be approved.
Privileged commands fail when approval or audit controls are unavailable.
Support access is read-only except for governed exception requests.

decisions.title: Define recovery and rehearsal before production handoff
decisions.selectedOption: Create a candidate recovery plan covering backup scope, routing-state restoration, failover ownership, core and batch restart, reconciliation and periodic rehearsal; objectives remain unresolved until supplied.
alternatives: Depend on existing platform backups without coexistence testing
Document recovery after the first wave
Treat rollback as the complete recovery strategy
decisions.rationale: The deterministic GOV-RECOVERY-DECISION finding requires an explicit recovery decision. CB-QR-003 also requires rehearsed recovery paths.
tradeoffs: Requires rehearsal time and representative environments.
Some external effects cannot be restored from backup.
Prevents unsupported recovery assumptions.
consequences: No recovery-time or recovery-point guarantee is claimed.
Authority-changing waves require passed recovery rehearsal evidence.
Rollback, failover and forward recovery are documented separately.

decisions.title: Require architecture handoff gates and ADR coverage
decisions.selectedOption: Do not treat this package as implementation approval; complete quality scenarios, ownership, topology, recovery and pattern/style review before production handoff.
alternatives: Proceed with incomplete review and fill gaps during delivery
Use meeting notes instead of ADRs
decisions.rationale: The AIW review reports incomplete measurable quality scenarios, no accepted ADR baseline and no approved pattern. The deterministic kernel requires human approval and prohibits LLM mutation or promotion.
tradeoffs: May slow initial handoff.
Reduces architecture drift and unsupported commitments.
Requires additional owner decisions.
consequences: All decisions in this package remain proposed candidates.
No Design Graph mutation or automatic promotion is performed.
Fitness evidence must be reviewed by authorized humans.

risks.description: A transaction or financial outcome is posted by both cores or replayed after an indeterminate result.
risks.mitigation: Enforce single-core authority, idempotency keys, destination status inquiry, duplicate detection and reconciliation before retry.

risks.description: Legacy and target customer, account, balance or transaction data diverge during migration.
risks.mitigation: Use versioned extracts, checkpoints, lineage, quarantined exceptions and independent pre/post-wave reconciliation.

risks.description: Cutover leaves routing, data and in-flight work in inconsistent states.
risks.mitigation: Use versioned state transitions, drain or classify in-flight work, checkpoint data, stop on partial execution and rehearse rollback and forward recovery.

risks.description: Unknown batch dependencies or overruns prevent end-of-day completion.
risks.mitigation: Inventory dependencies and cut-offs, migrate dependency-closed groups, block dependent jobs on indeterminate outcomes and rehearse restart procedures.

risks.description: Ledger or regulatory outputs are incomplete, duplicated or based on an incorrect source of authority.
risks.mitigation: Preserve Finance and Regulatory Reporting acceptance authority, carry lineage and reconcile transactions through postings and extracts before closure.

risks.description: Routing, migration or recovery activity disrupts customer access or produces unclear customer outcomes.
risks.mitigation: Preserve stable channel contracts, define transition service levels, use classified errors and correlation references, and provide support runbooks.

risks.description: Incomplete legacy interface and batch documentation causes hidden dependencies or incorrect transformations.
risks.mitigation: Run discovery, contract characterization, production-safe observation where authorized, dependency mapping and rehearsal before authority-changing waves.
risks.owner: Legacy core operations and Migration office

risks.description: Migration-state storage is unavailable, stale or corrupted, preventing safe routing.
risks.mitigation: Fail closed, use version checks and protected audit history, define backup and restoration, and exercise state-store recovery.

risks.description: Rollback is attempted after payment, ledger or reporting effects have become irreversible or indeterminate.
risks.mitigation: Define points of no return, track external outcomes separately, stop blind rollback and execute approved compensation or forward recovery.

risks.description: Privileged coexistence access bypasses segregation of duties or leaves insufficient audit evidence.
risks.mitigation: Use least privilege, maker-checker commands, time-bound emergency access, protected audit delivery and periodic access review.

delivery.executiveSummary: This candidate architecture replaces a big-bang core migration with governed account-level coexistence. Stable channel contracts feed a fail-closed router backed by versioned migration state; separate legacy and target facades isolate core semantics. Independent migration, reconciliation, financial integration, batch coordination, cutover orchestration, observability and security controls provide explicit ownership and failure paths. The approach is supported by the AIW deterministic preference for coarse-grained reversible evolution, but that recommendation has weak feasibility and is not an approval. Production handoff remains blocked by unresolved service-level thresholds, authority matrices, dependency discovery, recovery objectives, role assignments and pattern/ADR review.

sddSections.heading: Current-state diagnosis
sddSections.content: The estate spans channel APIs, payment rails, ledger posting, batch files and regulatory extracts. Legacy interface and batch documentation is incomplete, product dependencies constrain migration order, and financial obligations remain authoritative. A big-bang replacement is excluded. Exact coupling, service baselines, recovery objectives and data authority by state are not yet evidenced.

sddSections.heading: Target architecture
sddSections.content: Introduce a coarse-grained coexistence layer comprising stable channel access, account-state routing, legacy and target facades, controlled financial integrations, migration pipeline, independent reconciliation, cutover orchestration, batch coordination, operations telemetry, support workflow and cross-cutting security controls.

sddSections.heading: Transition states
sddSections.content: Use explicit LEGACY_AUTHORITY, COPY_IN_PROGRESS, SHADOW_VALIDATION, CUTOVER_PENDING, TARGET_AUTHORITY, ROLLBACK_PENDING and EXCEPTION states. State progression is versioned, approved, audited and stopped by failed or indeterminate gates.

sddSections.heading: Migration waves
sddSections.content: Wave 0 establishes discovery, contracts, controls and rehearsal without changing customer authority. Later waves consist only of dependency-closed cohorts derived from the validated product graph. Each wave requires data, security, operational, reconciliation, batch and service-level entry and exit evidence.

sddSections.heading: Cutover and rollback
sddSections.content: Cutover captures checkpoints, freezes conflicting state changes, classifies in-flight work, applies the final delta, reconciles, changes routing state and verifies outcomes. Rollback is allowed only before the defined point of no return and after restoration and reconciliation; otherwise use compensation or forward recovery.

sddSections.heading: Data strategy
sddSections.content: Define an authority matrix by entity and migration state, use stable identifiers and lineage, keep one active processing authority, make bulk loads restartable and idempotent, quarantine invalid records and independently reconcile through ledger and regulatory outcomes.

sddSections.heading: Security and operations
sddSections.content: Apply least privilege, maker-checker approvals, protected service identity, restricted bulk access, sensitive-data filtering and tamper-evident audit. Correlate technical and business telemetry and prevent authority-changing operations when required evidence is unavailable.

sddSections.heading: Governance status
sddSections.content: All elements and ADRs are candidate-only. CAMBRIDGE-SA-1.0 and the deterministic AIW rules inform the structure, while human approval is required. The compatibility Design Graph is unchanged and no pattern, decision or production state is promoted.

openIssues: Approve the data authority matrix for every entity and transition state.
Complete the legacy interface, batch, end-of-day and product dependency inventories.
Define and approve measurable transition service-level thresholds.
Define recovery objectives, backup scope, failover ownership and rehearsal criteria.
Define points of no return and compensation rules for payments, ledger and reporting.
Approve maker, checker, emergency-access and reconciliation-disposition roles.
Define data classification, retention and permitted use for migration and reconciliation evidence.
Materialize and review the canonical Design Graph before implementation handoff.
Review and accept or reject the proposed style and pattern choices with rationale.
implementationRoadmap: 1. Complete discovery: characterize interfaces, batch windows, product dependencies, authority rules and current service baselines.
2. Establish governance: approve owners, role separation, evidence policy, quality scenarios and recovery ADR.
3. Build stable channel and financial contracts plus legacy facades; deploy correlation, audit and observability without changing authority.
4. Implement the Migration Control Plane and fail-closed router; validate state recovery and routing contract tests.
5. Implement restartable migration and independent reconciliation with lineage and exception workflow.
6. Model batch and end-of-day dependencies and rehearse cross-estate recovery.
7. Execute Wave 0 rehearsals, including failed cutover, rollback and forward-recovery scenarios.
8. Select the first dependency-closed cohort only after all entry gates are accepted by authorized owners.
9. Run cohort waves with evidence-based review after each wave; retain long-tail exceptions in explicit states.
10. Decommission legacy capabilities only after routed, batch, financial, regulatory, security and recovery dependencies are evidenced as closed.
acceptanceAndFitnessTests: For every permitted migration state and operation, prove that the router selects the configured authoritative core and never invokes both cores.
Inject missing, stale, conflicting and unavailable migration state; verify fail-closed behavior, classified customer outcome and operational alert.
Repeat a transaction with the same idempotency identity; verify no duplicate accepted core, payment or ledger outcome.
Force an indeterminate core or external-destination response; verify status inquiry and reconciliation occur before retry, compensation or recovery.
For each wave, compare entity versions, balances, transactions, payment outcomes, ledger postings and regulatory extracts; verify missing or unexplained evidence blocks closure.
Rehearse cutover failure before the point of no return; verify checkpoint restoration, routing-state recovery, in-flight classification and post-rollback reconciliation.
Rehearse failure after an irreversible external effect; verify blind rollback is prohibited and the approved forward-recovery path is invoked.
Execute batch jobs with a missing prerequisite, overrun and indeterminate completion; verify dependent work and wave closure are stopped and owned runbooks are invoked.
Attempt a privileged migration-state change without maker-checker evidence or audit delivery; verify the command is denied.
Verify support users can view masked correlated evidence and create cases but cannot directly mutate balances, postings or routing state.
Verify telemetry correlates channel, routing, core, payment, ledger, batch and reconciliation events without logging prohibited sensitive fields.
Before each authority-changing wave, verify business and operational owners have approved measurable transition service-level thresholds and that rehearsal evidence meets them.
After recovery objectives are supplied, test backup restoration and failover for migration state, evidence and other in-scope components against those approved objectives.
Verify every major style, integration, data, resilience and security choice has a reviewed ADR before implementation handoff.

abstentions: No numeric availability, latency, recovery, capacity, reconciliation-tolerance or migration-duration guarantee is proposed because none is grounded.
No specific vendor product, cloud provider, database, messaging platform or deployment region is selected.
No named regulatory regime or jurisdiction-specific obligation is inferred.
No exact customer or product wave order is proposed before dependency discovery.
No assumption is made that all payment, ledger or reporting effects are reversible.
No pattern, ADR, architecture record or Design Graph element is accepted or promoted.
unsupportedClaimsRejected: Rejected a big-bang replacement because CB-C-001 explicitly prohibits it.
Rejected uncontrolled dual processing and target-first fallback because they could create dual posting or replay after an indeterminate outcome.
Rejected automatic migration-state promotion because the scenario requires governed cutover and the AIW authority policy requires human approval.
Rejected invented service-level and recovery targets under the unsupported-metric guard.
Rejected a claim that the architecture is production-ready because the AIW review identifies unresolved quality scenarios, ADR coverage and handoff readiness.
Rejected canonical Design Graph materialization because the supplied graph is only a compatibility projection and mutation is outside candidate authority.

problemUnderstanding.businessObjective: Deliver an enterprise agentic application that coordinates specialist capabilities and tools while bounding autonomy, data access, failure and cost.
scope: Accept user goals and construct governed, inspectable task plans.
Coordinate specialist capabilities using isolated identities and explicit delegation.
Invoke allowlisted enterprise tools only through a governed action boundary.
Manage tenant-scoped working memory and policy-governed durable memory.
Route high-impact, ambiguous and failed actions to human approval or intervention.
Capture audit evidence and evaluate quality, safety, latency, cost and policy outcomes.
Exclude direct model or agent mutation of approved enterprise state.
journeys: Candidate journey: an authenticated user submits a goal, receives a governed plan, and either receives an outcome or a classified failure.
Candidate journey: the orchestrator delegates bounded tasks to specialist capabilities without transferring user, tool or peer-agent privileges.
Candidate journey: a proposed tool action is authorized by deterministic policy and, when classified as high-impact, held until explicit human approval.
